Get a copy of your credit report. If anyone contacts you regarding debt, request a proof of debt in writing. For any entries on your credit report that won't supply proof of debt in writing, contest them via the credit bureaus.

This will force them to either show that you owe $x and provide information on how to pay it, or ignore you and let you contest the debt off of your credit report.

It sounds as if some debts have been sent or sold to collection agencies. It happened to us after a car accident. Some hospitals or private labs kick people to collections after a time, regardless of payment arrangements.

First rule - never do anything over the phone. Ever. In writing or it didn't happen. Also keep copies of paid invoices, checks, and so on. You may want to avoid changing banks in case you need old records of payments.

Second rule - know EXACTLY what you owe. Get and keep copies of hospital bills and treatment dates. What if a judge or a magistrate or a bankruptcy trustee wants to help settle your debts, but they need to know the original al charges, and all they have to go on is some collection agency and it's phony records padded with "late fees and finance charges"

Last, get help if you need it. Declaring bankruptcy over impossible debts really can clear your plate and let you start over. An attorney can also make sure all your debts and collections get settled so the bastards can never call you again.
